docs.title: Ktor-E-Commerce
docs.text: Ktor-E-Commerce is a high-performance backend solution designed for e-commerce applications built with ktor. This backend leverages the power of Kotlin to provide a robust, scalable, and efficient service for handling your e-commerce needs.

docs.title: Swagger View & API Discovery
docs.text:
Access interactive API documentation at the root / or /swagger endpoint when the application is running. The root URL automatically redirects to Swagger for easy API discovery for frontend developers and testers.

Every module has its own API page under API Reference, with methods, paths, access rules and request/response examples. Swagger UI remains the live contract generated from the route tree.

docs.title: 1. Role-Based Access Control
docs.text:
• Account types: Customer, Seller and Admin. SUPER_ADMIN is retained as a legacy value mapped to the platform super-admin role.
  • Database-backed roles: create custom roles, assign permissions and edit role bundles without a deploy.
  • Scoped permissions: platform roles (GLOBAL) and shop roles (SHOP) with resource:action codes.
  • Seller staff: shop memberships and invitations with owner, manager, catalog, fulfillment, inventory, finance, support, analyst, warehouse and POS roles.
  • Effective permissions: GET /api/v1/me/permissions returns roles, memberships and resolved permissions for UI rendering.
  • Least privilege: admin routes require explicit permissions; mixed customer/seller/admin routes guard admin access separately.
  • Audit: role, permission and membership changes are audited and bump authz_version to invalidate cached permissions.

See Users, Roles & Permissions for the model, permission catalog and API.

docs.title: 2. User Accounts and Authentication
docs.text:
• User Registration: Allow customers to create accounts. Users can register with the same email for different roles (customer and seller).
  • User Authentication: Implement JWT-based authentication for user sessions.
  • User Profiles: Enable users to view and update their profiles.

docs.title: 3. Product Management
docs.text:
• Product Listings: Create, update, and delete product listings.
  • Categories: Organize products into categories and brands for easy navigation.
  • Variants & Options: SKU/price/image per variant (Size, Color) with variant-level stock.
  • Recommendations: Related products, frequently-bought-together and personalized feeds.
  • Inventory Control: Multi-warehouse, variant-level stock with low-stock alerts.

docs.title: 4. Shopping Cart and Checkout
docs.text:
• Shopping Cart: Add and remove products, update quantities, and calculate totals.
  • Checkout Summary: Retrieve detailed checkout summary with subtotal, shipping, tax, and discount breakdown.
  • Checkout: Consolidated checkout process with integrated shipping address and method selection.
  • Cart Clearing: Automatic cart clearing after successful order placement.

docs.title: 5. Order Management
docs.text:
• Order Processing: Handle order creation with human-readable order numbers (ORD-YYYYMMDD-XXXX-XXXXXXXX).
  • Order Status History: Comprehensive audit trail for every status transition.
  • Automatic Taxation: Configurable tax calculation applied during checkout.
  • Order Cancellation: Cancel PENDING/CONFIRMED orders with automatic stock restoration.
  • Seller Orders: Sellers can view and manage orders from their shop.
  • Admin Orders: Admins can view all orders with advanced filters (status, date range).
  • Idempotency Support: Prevent duplicate orders with idempotency keys.
  • Payment Integration: Secure payment processing with amount validation.
  • Payment History: Track all payments for each order.

docs.title: 6. Discount & Coupon System
docs.text:
• Promo Codes: Create and manage fixed or percentage-based discount coupons.
  • Usage Limits: Enforce expiration dates, usage limits, and minimum order amounts.
  • Admin Controls: Dedicated administrative interface for managing the coupon lifecycle.

docs.title: 7. Refund Management
docs.text:
• Refund Requests: Customers can request refunds with reasons and evidence images.
  • Refund Approval: Sellers and admins can approve, reject, or process refunds.
  • Return Shipping: Track return shipments with tracking numbers.
  • Refund Lifecycle: Complete refund tracking from request to resolution.
  • RMA / Exchanges: Return or exchange delivered items with replacement-order linkage.

docs.title: 8. Seller Operations
docs.text:
• KYC: Business/bank verification gates payouts.
  • Payouts: Balance, request lifecycle, statements and CSV exports.
  • Warehouses: Split stock across physical locations.
  • Notifications: In-app inbox plus email/SMS/push providers with per-event preferences.
  • Tax & FX: Country/category tax rules and stored FX rates.

docs.title: 9. Platform Administration
docs.text:
• RBAC & API Keys: Granular permissions and scoped self-service keys.
  • Feature Flags: Runtime switches such as guest checkout.
  • Outbox & DLQ: Durable domain events with admin replay.
  • Audit Log: Immutable admin action trail.

docs.title: 10. Scalability and Performance
docs.text:
• Asynchronous Processing: Leverage Ktor's async capabilities for high performance.
  • Load Balancing: Easily scale your application to accommodate increased traffic.

docs.title: 11. Security
docs.text:
• JWT Tokens: Implement JSON Web Tokens for secure authentication.
  • Refresh Tokens: Secure token refresh with hashed storage and automatic revocation.
  • Rate Limiting: Auth endpoints protected against brute-force attacks (5 req/10min).
  • Account Lockout: Automatic 30-minute lockout after 5 failed login attempts.
  • Password Strength: Enforced password complexity requirements.
  • Input Validation: Protect against common web vulnerabilities like SQL injection and cross-site scripting (XSS).
  • Atomic Stock Operations: Thread-safe inventory updates within database transactions.
  • Health Checks: Comprehensive health monitoring with /health, /health/live, and /health/ready endpoints.
  • Structured Logging: Production-ready JSON logging with correlation IDs (Request IDs) for easier debugging and log aggregation.

docs.title: 12. Dashboard Analytics
docs.text:
• Summary Statistics: Quick overview of revenue, orders, users, products, and shops.
  • Revenue Analytics: Detailed revenue breakdown with daily trends and average order value.
  • Order Statistics: Order status distribution and recent order activity.
  • User Growth: User registration trends with breakdown by role and daily signups.
  • Top Products: Best-selling products ranked by sales volume and revenue.
  • Activity Feed: Recent platform activity including orders and user registrations.

docs.title: 13. Audit Logging
docs.text:
• Action Tracking: Records every admin action with actor identity, action type, and target resource.
  • Rich Context: Captures actor email, role, IP address, user agent, and outcome.
  • Filterable Queries: Search audit logs by actor, action type, resource, or outcome.
  • Immutable Records: Append-only log records for compliance.

docs.title: Architecture
docs.text:
Fig. Onion / Clean Architecture

The project follows Clean Architecture with clear separation of concerns:

  • Route Layer — HTTP routing only, uses by inject() for dependency injection
  • Service Layer — Business logic orchestration, works with domain models and DTOs
  • Repository Layer — Data access with Exposed queries and transaction management
  • Mapper Layer — Object mapping between DAO entities and response DTOs
  • Flyway — Version-controlled database migrations for safe schema management

docs.title: Environment Configuration
docs.text:
This project uses DotEnv for configuration management. Follow these steps to set up your environment:

  1. Create a .env file in the project root directory: 

       touch .env

  2. Add the following variables to your .env file:

   # Database Configuration
   DB_HOST=localhost
   DB_PORT=5432
   DB_NAME=ktor-ecommerce
   DB_USER=postgres
   DB_PASSWORD=p123

   # Server Configuration
   PORT=8080
   HOST=localhost

   # JWT Configuration
   JWT_SECRET=your-super-secret-jwt-secret-key-change-in-production
   JWT_ISSUER=ktor-ecommerce-app
   JWT_AUDIENCE=ktor-ecommerce
   JWT_REALM=ktor-ecommerce

   # Email Configuration
   EMAIL_HOST=smtp.gmail.com
   EMAIL_PORT=587
   EMAIL_USERNAME=your-email@gmail.com
   EMAIL_PASSWORD=your-gmail-app-password
  1. Update the values as needed for your environment, especially:
    • Database credentials to match your PostgreSQL setup
    • JWT secret with a strong, unique value for production
    • Email credentials with your actual Gmail and app password

The .env file is included in .gitignore to prevent sensitive information from being committed to the repository.

Note: For email configuration, make sure to use a Gmail app password rather than your regular Gmail password. You can generate an app password in your Google Account settings under Security > 2-Step Verification > App passwords.

docs.title: API Keys
docs.text: Create scoped API keys that inherit the owner's effective permissions.

docs.title: Endpoints
Effective permissions
docs.text:
A key can only receive scopes the owner currently holds. Scopes are re-checked against the owner's effective permissions on every authenticated request, so a role change narrows an existing key immediately.

Inspect the owner's roles and permissions with:

GET /api/v1/me/permissions

Platform admins should use /api/v1/admin/rbac/* to manage roles; see RBAC.

Keys can be revoked immediately; lookups use a hash of the key, never the plaintext. Revoking returns:

{ "message": "API key revoked" }

docs.text:
POST /api/v1/auth/social/google 
{ "idToken": "google-id-token", "mfaCode": "123456" }

The server verifies the token through Google's tokeninfo endpoint and checks:

  • email_verified = true
  • exp is in the future

Existing customers are matched by email; new verified customer accounts are created automatically and the Google sub is linked as the social identity. The response is the same token payload as password login.

docs.title: Passkeys (WebAuthn)
docs.text:
Passkeys enable passwordless login with platform authenticators.

  1. Start registration (authenticated):
curl -X POST 'http://localhost:8080/api/v1/auth/passkeys/register/options' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'
  1. Finish registration with the authenticator result:
{
  "credentialId": "base64url-credential-id",
  "clientDataJson": "base64url-client-data",
  "publicKey": "base64-spki-public-key",
  "name": "Laptop",
  "transports": ["internal"],
  "password": "current-password"
}

Passkey registration and deletion require step-up re-authentication. Supply the current password, or the current TOTP mfaCode when MFA is enabled. Accounts with MFA must supply a valid MFA code.

  1. Start login (public):
{ "email": "customer@example.com", "userType": "customer" }
  1. Finish login with the assertion:
{
  "email": "customer@example.com",
  "userType": "customer",
  "credentialId": "base64url-credential-id",
  "clientDataJson": "base64url-client-data",
  "authenticatorData": "base64url-authenticator-data",
  "signature": "base64url-signature",
  "mfaCode": "123456"
}

Validation:

  • challenge is single-use and expires after 5 minutes
  • ceremony type (webauthn.create / webauthn.get) and origin must match
  • ES256 signatures are verified against the stored SPKI public key
  • credentials are scoped to the owning user
  • when WEBAUTHN_REQUIRE_UV=true, the authenticator must assert user verification (UV)
  • passkey changes require recent password/MFA re-authentication

Configuration:

GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID=
WEBAUTHN_RP_ID=localhost
WEBAUTHN_RP_NAME=Ktor E-Commerce
WEBAUTHN_ORIGIN=http://localhost:3000
WEBAUTHN_REQUIRE_UV=false

Delete a passkey with a step-up body:

curl -X DELETE 'http://localhost:8080/api/v1/auth/passkeys/<id>' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"password":"current-password"}'

Passkey login returns the same access/refresh token pair as password login. When the account has TOTP MFA enabled, mfaCode is required. The authenticator RP-ID hash, user-presence flag and signature counter are validated; a counter regression is rejected. Attestation statement verification is intentionally left to the relying-party deployment; this API stores the registered SPKI key and verifies assertions.

docs.title: 28. Admin: clear login and OTP lockouts
Error Handling
docs.text: This API follows industry-standard error handling patterns (Stripe, GitHub, OpenAI):

docs.title: Success Responses
docs.text:
• HTTP status code indicates success (200, 201, 204)
  • Response body contains data directly (no wrapper object)
  • No isSuccess or statusCode fields needed

docs.title: Error Responses
docs.text:
Standard Error (400/401/403/404/500): 

{
  "message": "Error description"
}

Validation Error (400): 

{
  "message": "Validation failed",
  "errors": [
    {"field": "email", "message": "Invalid email format"},
    {"field": "password", "message": "Password must be at least 8 characters with uppercase, lowercase, digit, and special character"}
  ]
}

docs.title: Common Error Codes
docs.text:
Status Code Description Example Message 400 Bad Request "Invalid email or password" 401 Unauthorized "Authentication required" 403 Forbidden "Insufficient permissions" 404 Not Found "Product not found" 409 Conflict "User already exists with this email" 429 Too Many Requests "Rate limit exceeded. Try again later." 500 Internal Server Error "Internal server error"

All error messages are centralized and consistent across all endpoints.

docs.title: Rate Limiting
docs.text: Auth endpoints (login, register, forgot-password, reset-password) are rate-limited to 5 requests per 10 minutes per IP address. Exceeding this limit returns a 429 Too Many Requests response.

docs.title: Account Lockout
docs.text: After 5 consecutive failed login attempts, the account is automatically locked for 30 minutes. The login response includes remaining attempts count until the lockout is triggered.

docs.title: Password Strength
docs.text: All passwords must meet the following criteria: - Minimum 8 characters - At least one uppercase letter - At least one lowercase letter - At least one digit - At least one special character

docs.title: Multi-Factor Authentication (TOTP)
docs.text:
• RFC 6238 TOTP with SHA-1, 6 digits and a 30-second period
  • One time step of clock drift is accepted in either direction
  • The secret is generated server-side and stored AES-GCM encrypted (MFA_ENCRYPTION_KEY, falling back to JWT_SECRET in development); enable/disable requires a valid code
  • A TOTP time step can only be used once, preventing code replay within the 30-second window
  • When MFA is enabled, login must include mfaCode
  • Missing code returns 401 MFA_REQUIRED; an incorrect code returns 401 INVALID_MFA_CODE
  • Failed MFA attempts count toward the same 5-attempt lockout as bad passwords

docs.title: Refresh Token Security
docs.text:
• Refresh tokens are hashed before storage (SHA-256)
  • Tokens expire after 7 days
  • Each token refresh automatically revokes the old token and issues a new pair
  • Logout revokes all user refresh tokens

docs.title: Role Management
docs.text:
• Admin endpoints require both an ADMIN account and the relevant permission.
  • User type changes update the linked platform role assignment.
  • Deactivated users cannot log in but their data remains intact.
  • Activation restores account access; roles remain assigned.
  • Role and permission management lives under /api/v1/admin/rbac/*; see RBAC.

docs.title: Security Considerations
docs.text:
• Changing user types should be done carefully to maintain system security
  • Deactivation should be used for temporary account suspension
  • Regular monitoring of user type changes helps maintain security

docs.title: API Keys
docs.text:
API keys are scoped to a subset of the owner's effective permissions and are shown once at creation. Send them as Authorization: Bearer ek_....

Method Endpoint Description GET /api/v1/api-keys List your API keys (metadata only) POST /api/v1/api-keys Create a key (name, optional scopes, expiresAt) DELETE /api/v1/api-keys/{id} Revoke a key

Scopes accept permission codes (order:manage, inventory:manage) or legacy enum names (ORDER_MANAGE, INVENTORY_MANAGE). Keys are re-checked against the owner's current effective permissions at authentication, so a role change narrows an existing key.

Feature flags require feature_flag:manage; see RBAC.

docs.title: B2B Quotes, Purchase Orders & Net Terms
docs.text: Wholesale accounts, quotes, purchase orders, credit limits and net-term invoices.

docs.title: Endpoints
docs.text: Method Endpoint Description Authentication Required POST /api/v1/b2b/account Apply for or update a B2B account Yes POST /api/v1/b2b/quotes Request a B2B quote Yes PUT /api/v1/seller/b2b/quotes/{id} Seller: price and send/reject a quote Yes (Seller) POST /api/v1/b2b/quotes/{id}/accept Accept a quote and create a purchase order Yes

docs.title: 1. Accounts
2. Quotes
3. Purchase orders and net terms
docs.text:
POST /api/v1/b2b/quotes/{id}/accept
  • Available credit = creditLimit - open purchase orders.
  • Creates an OPEN purchase order with a unique PO number.
  • Sets dueDate = now + paymentTermsDays.
  • Marks the quote ACCEPTED.

Buyer:

  • GET /api/v1/b2b/purchase-orders
  • GET /api/v1/b2b/purchase-orders/{id}

Seller:

  • GET /api/v1/seller/b2b/purchase-orders
  • POST /api/v1/seller/b2b/purchase-orders/{id}/fulfill — creates the buyer order, decrements stock, links the PO to the order and sets FULFILLED

Admin:

  • GET /api/v1/admin/b2b/accounts?status=APPROVED
  • PUT /api/v1/admin/b2b/accounts/{userId}
  • GET /api/v1/admin/b2b/purchase-orders

PO statuses: OPEN → FULFILLED; CANCELED is reserved for future cancellation flows. The PO response includes the generated orderId after fulfillment.

docs.title: Invoices and dunning
docs.text:
Fulfilling a PO creates a net-terms invoice (PENDING) with a unique invoice number and the PO due date.

Buyer / seller / admin:

  • GET /api/v1/b2b/invoices
  • GET /api/v1/seller/b2b/invoices
  • GET /api/v1/admin/b2b/invoices

Admin actions:

  • POST /api/v1/admin/b2b/invoices/run-dunning — marks due invoices OVERDUE, increments the reminder count and schedules the next reminder in 7 days. Returns { "reminded": N }.
  • POST /api/v1/admin/b2b/invoices/{id}/pay?providerReference=wire-123 — records settlement, marks the invoice PAID, and marks the linked order payment COMPLETED (and PAID while it is still PENDING/CONFIRMED).

Invoice statuses: PENDING → OVERDUE → PAID; VOID is reserved for cancellation/credit-note flows.

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
• Quote items must be positive quantities.
  • Unit prices must be positive.
  • Credit limit cannot be negative; terms must be positive.
  • The platform tracks net-terms invoices and reminders but does not auto-charge bank transfers; settlement remains an accounting/ERP integration.

Other operations:

  • POST /api/v1/admin/b2b/invoices/{id}/void — Admin: void an unpaid B2B invoice
  • POST /api/v1/seller/b2b/purchase-orders/{id}/cancel — Seller: cancel an open purchase order

docs.text: Shipping addresses, shipping methods, summaries and order placement.

docs.title: Consolidated Workflow
docs.text: All endpoints are under /api/v1/checkout and require CUSTOMER authentication, except POST /api/v1/checkout/guest which is public and feature-flagged (guest_checkout).

docs.title: 0. Guest Checkout (feature-flagged)
docs.text:
POST /api/v1/checkout/guest

Places an order without an account. The request may include a guest email; if an account with that email already exists the order is claimed by it. Disabled when the guest_checkout feature flag is off.

Request: 

{
  "email": "guest@example.com",
  "firstName": "Guest",
  "lastName": "Shopper",
  "phoneNumber": "+8801700000000",
  "streetAddress": "12 Main St",
  "city": "Dhaka",
  "country": "BD",
  "postCode": "1207",
  "shippingMethodId": "uuid",
  "paymentMethod": "COD",
  "currency": "USD",
  "items": [{ "productId": "uuid", "quantity": 1 }]
}

Returns 201 Created with the created order(s).

docs.title: 1. Manage Shipping Address
docs.text:
• POST /api/v1/checkout/shipping-address: Add a new address.
  • GET /api/v1/checkout/shipping-address: List saved addresses.
  • PUT /api/v1/checkout/shipping-address/{id}: Update address.
  • DELETE /api/v1/checkout/shipping-address/{id}: Remove address.

docs.title: 2. Shipping Methods
docs.text: • GET /api/v1/checkout/shipping-method: Retrieve available shipping options (Standard, Express, etc.).

docs.title: 3. Order Summary (Real-time Calculation)
docs.text:
POST /api/v1/checkout/summary

Calculate totals, taxes, and apply coupons without creating an order. Use this to show the final price to the customer before they confirm.

Request: 

{
  "shippingAddressId": "uuid",
  "shippingMethodId": "uuid",
  "couponCode": "DISCOUNT10"
}

Response: 

{
  "subTotal": "100.00",
  "shippingCost": "15.00",
  "taxAmount": "5.00",
  "discountAmount": "10.00",
  "total": "110.00",
  "itemCount": 3
}

docs.title: 4. Place Order
docs.text:
POST /api/v1/checkout/place-order

Finalizes the purchase and creates order records. Send Idempotency-Key (or the body idempotencyKey) to make retries safe; totals are server-validated against database prices.

Request: 

{
  "shippingAddressId": "uuid",
  "shippingMethodId": "uuid",
  "paymentMethod": "CREDIT_CARD",
  "notes": "Leave at the door",
  "couponCode": "DISCOUNT10",
  "usePoints": 500,
  "walletCredit": 10.00,
  "giftCardCode": "GIFT1234ABCD",
  "locale": "fr",
  "attribution": {"sessionId":"sess_123","source":"google","medium":"cpc","campaign":"spring"},
  "idempotencyKey": "unique-uuid-per-attempt"
}

Response: A list of created orders (split by shop if multi-vendor).

docs.title: Guest Checkout
docs.text:
POST /api/v1/checkout/guest places an order without an account. It is gated by the guest_checkout feature flag (disabled by default; enable via the super-admin feature-flags API).

A guest order creates an unverified guest CUSTOMER for the checkout email. If that email later registers and verifies the OTP, the account (and order history) is claimed. Guest orders can be tracked with GET /api/v1/orders/track?orderNumber=...&email=....

Other operations:

  • POST /api/v1/checkout/guest/summary — Guest checkout quote

docs.title: Error Handling & Status Codes
docs.text: All API endpoints in Ktor-E-Commerce adhere to consistent, RESTful error handling principles modeled after industry standards (such as Stripe, GitHub, and RFC 7807 Problem Details).

docs.title: Response Envelope Philosophy
docs.text:
• Direct Data on Success: Successful requests return the domain payload or resource array directly (HTTP 200, 201, or 204 No Content). No redundant { "isSuccess": true, "data": ... } wrapping.
  • Structured JSON on Failure: Whenever a client or server error occurs (HTTP 4xx or 5xx), a uniform JSON error payload is returned with human-readable messaging and contextual validation errors.

docs.title: Standard Error Schema
docs.text:
For general errors (e.g. 401 Unauthorized, 403 Forbidden, 404 Not Found, 409 Conflict, 500 Internal Server Error), the response schema is:

{
  "message": "Resource not found"
}

docs.title: Validation Error Schema (HTTP 400)
docs.text:
When incoming request parameters, path variables, or body fields fail validation rules (e.g., format violations, missing required fields, or constraint failures), an errors array provides field-level feedback:

{
  "message": "Validation failed",
  "errors": [
    {
      "field": "email",
      "message": "Invalid email format"
    },
    {
      "field": "password",
      "message": "Password must be at least 8 characters"
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: HTTP Status Codes Reference
docs.text:
The following HTTP status codes are systematically returned across all API endpoints:

Status Code Meaning Typical Trigger Example Message 200 OK Success Resource retrieved or updated successfully N/A (Payload returned) 201 Created Resource Created New entity successfully persisted N/A (Created entity returned) 204 No Content Success (No Body) Resource deleted or action completed without return body Empty 400 Bad Request Validation / Client Error Malformed JSON, missing mandatory fields, invalid parameters "Invalid email or password" 401 Unauthorized Missing / Expired Auth Missing or expired JWT access token in Authorization header "Authentication required" 403 Forbidden Insufficient Permissions Valid identity, but account type or assigned RBAC permissions lack access "Insufficient permissions" 404 Not Found Resource Missing Non-existent ID or unmapped route path "Product not found" 409 Conflict State Conflict Duplicate unique key (e.g., user email already registered, SKU duplicate) "User already exists with this email" 422 Unprocessable Business Rule Failure Syntactically correct input violating business constraints (e.g., insufficient stock) "Requested quantity exceeds available stock" 429 Too Many Requests Rate Limit Exceeded Auth or checkout brute-force limits triggered "Too many requests. Please try again later." 500 Internal Server Error Server Fault Unexpected unhandled exception logged with request correlation ID "Internal server error"

docs.title: Client Error Handling Guidelines
docs.text:
1. Check the HTTP Status First: Differentiate between client remediation (4xx) and system degradation (5xx).
  2. Inspect Field-Level Errors: If status is 400 Bad Request, check if the errors array is present to map inline validation messages directly to UI form inputs.
  3. Handle Token Expiration: When receiving 401 Unauthorized, trigger the token refresh flow (POST /api/v1/auth/refresh-token) before retrying the original request.
  4. Idempotency on Network Failure: For mutating requests (like placing an order or charging a payment), pass the Idempotency-Key header to safely retry without duplicate transactions.

docs.title: Velocity rules
docs.text:
Metrics:

  • ORDER_COUNT — orders placed by the customer in the window
  • ORDER_AMOUNT — sum of order totals in the window
  • PAYMENT_ATTEMPTS — payment rows created in the window

Actions:

  • ALLOW — record only
  • REVIEW — allow the payment but flag it for manual review
  • REQUIRE_3DS — ask the card provider to enforce 3-D Secure
  • BLOCK — reject the payment before the provider is called (403 FRAUD_BLOCKED)
{
  "name": "More than 5 orders/hour",
  "metric": "ORDER_COUNT",
  "windowMinutes": 60,
  "threshold": 5,
  "action": "REVIEW",
  "priority": 10,
  "isActive": true
}

The highest-priority matching rules are evaluated; BLOCK wins over REVIEW, which wins over REQUIRE_3DS.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Ktor-E-Commerce provides dedicated health check endpoints outside the /api/v1 version prefix. These are designed for load balancers, orchestrator readiness probes, and synthetic monitoring without incurring authentication overhead.

docs.title: Health Check Endpoints
docs.text: Method Endpoint Purpose Upstream Checks Typical HTTP Status GET /health Basic application ping Application runtime 200 OK GET /health/live Kubernetes Liveness probe Application process active 200 OK GET /health/ready Kubernetes Readiness probe Database connection pool (SELECT 1) 200 OK or 503 Service Unavailable

docs.title: 1. Application Liveness
docs.text:
GET /health/live Public / No Auth Required

Verifies the JVM process is accepting HTTP traffic. Used by orchestrators to determine whether the container needs a restart.

docs.title: 2. Database Readiness Probe

GET /health/ready Public / No Auth Required

Executes an active test query (SELECT 1) against the PostgreSQL database connection pool with a 3,000 ms timeout. If the database is unreachable or connection pools are exhausted, the endpoint responds with 503 Service Unavailable so the load balancer temporarily diverts traffic.

    port: 8080
  initialDelaySeconds: 10
  periodSeconds: 15
  timeoutSeconds: 3

docs.title: Points
docs.text:
• Earn 1 point per 1 USD of a paid order (LOYALTY_POINTS_PER_USD).
  • Redeem 100 points = 1 USD (LOYALTY_POINTS_PER_USD_REDEEM).
  • Earnings are idempotent per order; replaying a payment confirmation does not double-award.
  • Points are awarded when the order becomes fully paid.
  • Points are earned on the USD-normalized order total.
  • Cancellation/full refund reverses earned points, restores redeemed points/store credit and refunds gift-card redemptions back to the card.

Checkout body:

{
  "shippingAddressId": "address-uuid",
  "shippingMethodId": "method-uuid",
  "paymentMethod": "CREDIT_CARD",
  "usePoints": 500,
  "walletCredit": 10.00,
  "giftCardCode": "GIFT1234ABCD"
}

walletCredit is in USD and is converted with the order FX rate. Redemptions are applied after coupons/promotions and capped at the order total before points/credit are debited, so unused balances are never burned. Points/credit/gift-card debits are recorded in wallet_ledger/gift_card_redemption and the order stores walletDiscount and giftCardDiscount.

Checkout summary returns walletDiscount, giftCardDiscount, pointsBalance and storeCreditBalance so clients can display the applied amounts before placing the order.

docs.text:
Each wallet has a unique referralCode.

  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{ "code": "REF12345" }'
  • Self-referral and duplicate claims are rejected.
  • The referral stays PENDING until the referee's first order is paid.
  • On completion both sides receive REFERRAL_REWARD_POINTS (default 100) as a REFERRAL_BONUS ledger entry.
  • A user can be a referee only once.

  "amount": 50.00,
  "currency": "USD",
  "code": "GIFT1234ABCD",

code is optional; a unique 16-character code is generated when omitted. Codes are case-insensitive on redemption. Partial redemptions reduce the balance; a zero balance marks the card REDEEMED. Voided, expired and non-USD cards cannot be redeemed. Unused balance stays on the card.

docs.title: 9. Provider Webhook
docs.text:
POST /api/v1/payments/webhook/{provider}

300 seconds and can be tuned with STRIPE_WEBHOOK_TOLERANCE_SECONDS. - Other adapters can use X-Webhook-Signature. - Deliveries are deduplicated by (provider, event_id), so retries are safe. - payment_intent.succeeded completes the payment and marks the order PAID once the total is covered; payment_intent.payment_failed marks it FAILED. - refund.updated mirrors the processor refund status onto the refund request.

curl -X 'POST' \
  'http://localhost:8080/api/v1/payments/webhook/stripe' \
  -H 'Stripe-Signature: t=1700000000,v1=<signature>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"id":"evt_1","type":"payment_intent.succeeded","data":{"object":{"id":"pi_1","status":"succeeded"}}}'

Invalid signatures return 400; duplicate deliveries return 200. Processing failures return a 5xx so the provider retries rather than the event being permanently dropped.

docs.text:
Variable Description PAYMENT_PROVIDER manual (COD only, default) or stripe STRIPE_SECRET_KEY Stripe secret key; required when the provider is stripe STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET Signing secret used to verify webhooks STRIPE_BASE_URL API base URL (override for tests/proxies) STRIPE_WEBHOOK_TOLERANCE_SECONDS Maximum accepted clock skew for webhook signatures

POST /api/v1/payments also accepts returnUrl (where the customer returns after 3DS). Responses include provider, providerReference, clientSecret, nextActionUrl, scaStatus and providerStatus. A payment remains PENDING while scaStatus is REQUIRED/PENDING.

docs.text:

Orders and payments are retained in pseudonymous form for financial/legal obligations; direct identifiers, addresses, carts, wishlists, reviews, consents and notifications are removed or anonymized.

docs.title: Data Retention & Privacy Operations
docs.text: This document defines the intended retention and deletion policy for personal data. It must be reviewed by legal/accounting before production use.

docs.title: Principles
docs.text:
• Collect only what is needed for the order, account, payment, tax and support flows.
  • Pseudonymize or anonymize when the business purpose ends.
  • Retain financial/tax records only as long as legally required.
  • Never use deleted-account data for marketing or analytics.
  • Backups follow the same retention schedule and are not selectively edited.

docs.title: Recommended retention
docs.text: Data category Default retention Notes Active account/profile While account is active Erasure request starts anonymization Orders, payments, refunds, invoices, payouts, tax 7 years after the financial year Accounting/tax/chargeback obligations Shipping addresses on orders 7 years Needed for disputes/returns; direct identifiers may be redacted Support tickets/messages 3 years after closure Remove/anonymize on erasure unless needed for a dispute Analytics events 13 months Aggregate reports may be kept longer without identifiers Webhook inbox payloads (payment/carrier) 90 days Retain only the processing status after that Notification inbox 1 year User-deletable Cart, wishlist, browsing data While active / 30 days idle Deleted on erasure Passkeys and social identities Until removed or account erased Credentials are deleted on erasure Wallet ledger / gift-card redemptions 7 years Financial audit trail; account identifiers pseudonymized B2B accounts/quotes/POs 7 years Contract/tax records Seller reviews/disputes 3 years after resolution Anonymize author on erasure Audit logs 2 years Security/legal investigations Backups 35 days rolling Not selectively editable

docs.title: Erasure exceptions
docs.text:
Account erasure anonymizes the account and removes self-service data. The following may be retained in pseudonymous form where required:

  • orders, payments, refunds, invoices, tax and payout records
  • chargeback/dispute evidence
  • fraud/security records required for investigations
  • records subject to a legal hold

Support tickets, passkeys, wallet account/ledger, digital entitlements, analytics events and social identities are removed or anonymized. Order contact PII and delivery snapshots are cleared.

docs.title: Data-subject requests
docs.text:
• Export endpoint returns account/profile, addresses, orders, payments, refunds, consents, reviews, notifications and additional wallet/subscription/support/passkey/B2B/analytics metadata.
  • Erasure requires the account password and revokes all refresh tokens.
  • Operators should record DSAR completion in the audit log.

docs.title: Operational jobs
docs.text:
MaintenanceCleanup runs daily and currently:

  • purges published outbox rows, expired/revoked refresh tokens and expired blacklisted tokens
  • purges old login/OTP counters and read notifications
  • purges payment and carrier webhook inbox payloads older than 90 days
  • purges analytics events older than 13 months
  • deletes expired digital entitlements
  • deletes cart items idle for more than 30 days
  • deletes resolved support tickets (and cascaded messages) older than 3 years
  • deletes expired WebAuthn ceremony challenges

Still recommended:

  • expire/clear stale wishlists
  • run the documented legal-hold review before deleting financial records

docs.title: Open decisions
docs.text:
• Exact jurisdiction-specific financial retention periods.
  • Whether wallet ledgers must be retained after erasure (currently deleted).
  • Whether support transcripts must be retained for dispute/legal holds.
  • Backup restore procedures for re-applying erasure requests.

docs.title: Cart and checkout
docs.text:
• When a product has variants, POST /api/v1/carts requires variantId; adding the base product is rejected.
  • Cart lines are unique per (user, product, variant), so several variants of one product can coexist.
  • Checkout uses the variant price, SKU, name and variant-level stock; order items snapshot variantId and variantName.
  • Cancellations, refunds and RMA replacements restore stock to the purchased variant.

docs.title: Users, roles and permissions
docs.text:
Database-backed roles, permissions, seller memberships and invitations.

Status: foundation implemented (schema, effective-permission resolution, platform role APIs, seller membership APIs).

Scope: platform operators, sellers and customers. B2B company memberships are intentionally out of scope for this phase.

docs.title: 1. Model
docs.text:
Authorization is split into three layers:

Layer Question Stored in Account type What kind of identity is this? "user".user_type Membership Which shop/platform does the user act in? shop_member, auth_user_role Role + permission What may they do? auth_role, auth_permission, auth_role_permission

docs.title: Account types
docs.text:
CUSTOMER
SELLER
ADMIN

Rules:

  • ADMIN only grants access to the admin console. Permissions come from roles.
  • SUPER_ADMIN is retained as a legacy enum value and mapped to the platform:super_admin role. It will be removed after existing rows and clients are migrated.
  • Guest checkout uses user.is_guest, not an account type.
  • Staff is never an account type. A staff member is user + membership + role.

docs.title: 2. Tables
docs.text: Table Purpose auth_permission Permission catalog (resource:action) auth_role Platform (GLOBAL) and shop (SHOP) roles auth_role_permission Role → permission mapping auth_user_role Platform role assignment shop_member User membership in a shop shop_member_role Shop role assignment shop_invitation Pending staff invitation (token hash, expiry) member_warehouse Optional warehouse scoping for shop staff "user".authz_version Invalidates cached permissions

docs.title: 3. Permission codes
docs.text:
The existing Permission enum now carries a stable code:

Enum Code USER_MANAGE user:manage CATALOG_MANAGE catalog:manage ORDER_MANAGE order:manage PAYMENT_MANAGE payment:manage REFUND_MANAGE refund:manage PAYOUT_MANAGE payout:manage COUPON_MANAGE coupon:manage SHOP_MANAGE shop:manage INVENTORY_MANAGE inventory:manage POLICY_MANAGE policy:manage DASHBOARD_VIEW dashboard:read AUDIT_VIEW audit:read NOTIFICATION_SEND notification:send TAX_MANAGE tax:manage FX_MANAGE fx:manage OUTBOX_MANAGE outbox:manage API_KEY_MANAGE api_key:manage FEATURE_FLAG_MANAGE feature_flag:manage ROLE_MANAGE role:manage SUPPORT_MANAGE support:manage FRAUD_MANAGE fraud:manage CMS_MANAGE cms:manage SUBSCRIPTION_MANAGE subscription:manage REVIEW_MANAGE review:manage SHIPPING_MANAGE shipping:manage B2B_MANAGE b2b:manage

Custom roles may include codes that do not have an enum constant yet. Route gates still use enum constants, so new route-level checks require a code constant; business-level checks can use raw codes through the resolver.

docs.title: 4. Effective permissions
docs.text:
effective(user) =
  union(permissions of active platform roles)
  ∪ union(permissions of active shop memberships)

Rules:

  • If the user has no assignments, the legacy UserType.defaultPermissions() mapping is used for customers and sellers. This keeps existing behavior working.
  • Platform admins are the exception: an ADMIN/SUPER_ADMIN with no role assignment gets no permissions, so an orphaned admin can never fall back to full access.
  • If the user has any assignment, the result is exact. An assigned role with no permissions grants nothing.
  • Results are cached by userId + authz_version for 60 seconds.
  • Any role assignment or membership change increments authz_version, so the next request resolves fresh permissions.

docs.title: 5. Authentication flow
docs.text:
ConfigureAuth now:

  1. Validates the JWT and loads the user from the database.
  2. Resolves effective permissions through RbacService.
  3. Builds JwtTokenRequest with permissions and authzVersion.

JwtTokenRequest.hasPermission():

  • JWT: checks the resolved permission set (code or legacy enum name).
  • API key: checks explicit scopes (legacy enum names or codes).
  • Fallback: role defaults only when no resolved set was supplied.

API keys are validated against the owner's effective permissions at creation and at authentication, so a role change narrows an existing key.

docs.title: 8. Migration
docs.text:
V66__rbac_and_seller_members.sql:

  1. Adds user.authz_version.
  2. Creates the RBAC and shop-membership tables.
  3. Seeds the permission catalog and all system roles.
  4. Backfills SUPER_ADMIN → platform:super_admin.
  5. Backfills ADMIN → platform:admin.
  6. Creates owner memberships for existing sellers with a shop.

V67__b2b_permission.sql adds the b2b:manage permission and grants it to platform:admin and platform:super_admin.

Backward compatibility:

  • Existing admin JWTs keep working because permissions are resolved server-side.
  • Existing API keys keep working because scopes accept both enum names and codes.
  • SUPER_ADMIN remains accepted by adminAuth until the enum value is retired.

docs.title: 9. Admin route gates
docs.text:
The following admin groups now require explicit permissions instead of relying on adminAuth alone:

Group Permission admin/auth, admin/users user:manage admin/rbac role:manage admin/brands, categories, products catalog:manage admin/inventories inventory:manage admin/orders order:manage admin/payments, webhooks, gift cards, wallets payment:manage admin/refunds, admin/rma-requests refund:manage admin/payouts, commission rules payout:manage admin/fraud, admin/chargebacks fraud:manage admin/support/tickets, admin/disputes support:manage admin/cms, admin/seo cms:manage admin/policies, policy consents policy:manage admin/shipping-methods shipping:manage admin/subscriptions, plans subscription:manage admin/reviews, seller reviews review:manage admin/feature-flags feature_flag:manage admin/outbox outbox:manage admin/tax-* tax:manage admin/fx-rates fx:manage admin/audit-logs audit:read admin/dashboard, queues, analytics dashboard:read admin/b2b b2b:manage

Mixed customer/seller/admin routes use requireAdminPermission(...) so a narrowly-scoped admin cannot bypass the permission gate through a customer or seller endpoint. sellerAuth is exact SELLER only; admins use the admin console.

docs.title: 10. Behavior changes from the old model
docs.text:
• sellerAuth now allows exact SELLER accounts only. Admins use the admin console instead of inheriting seller routes.
  • Customer order detail, refund evidence and invoice routes no longer give admins implicit access. Admin access is checked with requireAdminPermission(...) (order:manage / refund:manage) or through the admin routes.
  • notifications/send requires notification:send instead of any admin/seller role.
  • Feature flags now require feature_flag:manage; a plain ADMIN no longer gets implicit access (only SUPER_ADMIN/platform:developer do).
  • Invoice, packing-slip and shipment endpoints require order:manage for admin principals.
  • B2B admin routes require b2b:manage.
  • Changing a role's permissions increments authz_version for every holder of that role, so cached permissions are invalidated immediately.

docs.title: 11. Known limitations / next phase
docs.text:
• Seller service authorization still uses requireSellerByUserId and sellerOwnsShop. Invited staff have a membership, but seller endpoints that require a seller row will reject them. The next phase is to replace those checks with requireShopPermission(user, shopId, permission).
  • Invited staff should be SELLER accounts to enter the seller center in this phase. A CUSTOMER invitee can accept and receive a membership, but the seller portal gate will reject them until membership-based portal access lands.
  • Route gates are still coarse (CATALOG_MANAGE, not catalog:read / catalog:write). Granular route gates can be added incrementally.
  • platform:finance_approver and platform:finance_payer currently share the coarse payout:manage code. Split into payout:approve and payout:pay when payout endpoints are migrated.
  • Invitation emails are not sent yet; the token is returned by the API.
  • SUPER_ADMIN should be removed from UserType after a data backfill and client migration.
  • B2B company memberships are out of scope.

docs.title: 12. Code layout
docs.text:
File Responsibility RbacModels.kt API request/response DTOs RbacService.kt Permission resolution, roles, platform assignments ShopMembershipService.kt Shop staff memberships and invitations RbacSupport.kt Shared role/member lookup and mapping helpers constants/Rbac.kt Role scope, membership/invitation status and seeded ids RbacRoutes.kt Admin, seller member, /me and invitation routes

Shared utilities: utils/common/Hashing.kt and Iterable<String>.entityIDs(...) in StringExt.kt.

docs.title: 13. Verification
docs.text:
• ./gradlew build passes: 637 tests, 0 failures.
  • mkdocs build --strict passes.
  • The module API pages and Swagger UI cover 464 operations / 47 tags, including the 16 RBAC operations.
  • ./gradlew detekt reports only the four pre-existing structural warnings.

  • platform:admin intentionally excludes feature_flag:manage.
  • RbacPrincipalTest covers permission codes, resolved permission checks, legacy fallback and API-key scopes.

docs.text:

docs.text:
Carrier quotes, label purchase, fulfillment and tracking webhooks.

All endpoints except the tracking webhook require Bearer authentication. A customer may read their own order's shipments; sellers may quote and purchase labels for their shop; admins may do both for any order.

docs.title: 1. Rate quote
2. Purchase a label
docs.text:
POST /api/v1/orders/{id}/shipments 
{
  "rateId": "rate_123",
  "items": [
    { "orderItemId": "item-uuid", "quantity": 1 }
  ]
}

Response (201 Created):

{
  "id": "shipment-uuid",
  "orderId": "order-uuid",
  "carrier": "USPS",
  "service": "Priority Mail",
  "trackingNumber": "9400111",
  "labelUrl": "https://labels.example/shipment.pdf",
  "rateAmount": "7.50",
  "currency": "USD",
  "status": "LABEL_PURCHASED",
  "shippedAt": "2026-05-01T10:00:00Z",
  "deliveredAt": null,
  "createdAt": "2026-05-01T10:00:00Z",
  "items": [{ "orderItemId": "item-uuid", "quantity": 1 }]
}

Rules:

  • The order must be PAID (or already partly SHIPPED).
  • A line cannot ship more than ordered - already shipped.
  • When every unit is allocated, the order becomes SHIPPED and gets the latest tracking number.
  • Over-shipping and non-seller callers are rejected.
  • idempotencyKey is optional; a retry with the same key returns the original label instead of buying a second one.

docs.title: Admin webhook replay
docs.text:
• GET /api/v1/admin/webhooks?source=CARRIER&status=FAILED
  • POST /api/v1/admin/webhooks/carriers/{id}/replay

Stored carrier payloads can be re-applied after fixing a mapping/outage. Replay updates the inbox row and writes an audit entry; it does not require the original signature.

docs.title: 4. Tracking webhook
docs.text:
POST /api/v1/shipments/webhook/{provider}
  • Deliveries are deduplicated by (provider, event_id); the event ID is the SHA-256 of the payload, so retries are safe.
  • TRANSIT/OUT_FOR_DELIVERY → IN_TRANSIT
  • DELIVERED → DELIVERED; the order becomes DELIVERED once every parcel is delivered.
  • RETURNED → RETURNED; FAILURE/EXPIRED → FAILED.
curl -X 'POST' \
  'http://localhost:8080/api/v1/shipments/webhook/shippo' \
  -H 'X-Carrier-Signature: <hmac-or-shared-secret>' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"event":"track_updated","data":{"tracking_number":"9400111","tracking_status":{"status":"DELIVERED"}}}'

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Variable Description SHIPPING_PROVIDER manual (default) or shippo SHIPPO_API_TOKEN Shippo token; required when the provider is shippo SHIPPO_BASE_URL API base URL (override for tests/proxies) CARRIER_WEBHOOK_SECRET HMAC/shared secret for tracking webhooks

With manual, rate quotes are empty and label purchase is unavailable; sellers can still use POST /api/v1/orders/{id}/shipping with a manually entered tracking number.

docs.title: Subscriptions & Digital Goods
docs.text: Recurring plans, invoices and digital download entitlements.

docs.title: Plans
docs.text:
A plan is attached to a digital product and bills monthly or yearly.

{
  "name": "Pro Monthly",
  "description": "Monthly access to the Pro pack",
  "productId": "product-uuid",
  "interval": "MONTH",
  "price": 9.99,
  "currency": "USD",
  "trialDays": 0,
  "isActive": true
}

Public: GET /api/v1/subscription-plans?productId=...

Admin CRUD:

  • GET /api/v1/admin/subscription-plans
  • POST /api/v1/admin/subscription-plans
  • PUT /api/v1/admin/subscription-plans/{id}
  • DELETE /api/v1/admin/subscription-plans/{id} — deactivates

docs.title: Endpoints
docs.text: Method Endpoint Description Authentication Required POST /api/v1/subscriptions Subscribe to a plan Yes POST /api/v1/admin/subscriptions/run-billing Create renewal invoices for due subscriptions Yes (Admin) POST /api/v1/admin/subscriptions/{id}/activate Admin: mark a pending subscription invoice paid and activate Yes (Admin) GET /api/v1/library List my digital purchases Yes GET /api/v1/library/{token}/download Redeem a digital download Yes

docs.title: 1. Subscribing
docs.text:
POST /api/v1/subscriptions 
{
  "planId": "plan-uuid",
  "paymentReference": "pay_123",
  "paymentMethodReference": "pm_123",
  "providerCustomerReference": "cus_123"
}
  • With a paymentReference, creates an ACTIVE subscription with a paid invoice.
  • Without a reference, creates a PENDING subscription and a PENDING invoice; no entitlement is granted until payment is recorded.
  • paymentMethodReference / providerCustomerReference are provider tokens, not card data. They enable off-session renewal charges with PAYMENT_PROVIDER=stripe. Never send raw card numbers.
  • Period starts now and ends after one month/year (plus trial days).
  • Grants a digital entitlement when the plan’s product is digital and payment is confirmed.
  • Rejects duplicate active subscriptions for the same plan.

Other endpoints:

  • GET /api/v1/subscriptions
  • GET /api/v1/subscriptions/{id}/invoices
  • POST /api/v1/subscriptions/{id}/cancel — marks cancelAtPeriodEnd

docs.title: 2. Renewal billing
Digital goods
docs.text:
Products can be marked digital:

{
  "isDigital": true,
  "digitalAssetUrl": "https://downloads.example/pack.zip",
  "digitalFileName": "pack.zip"
}

Digital-only orders have zero shipping cost and the order shipping method is stored as DIGITAL. When payment completes, an entitlement is created for each digital product in the order.

docs.title: 3. Library
docs.text:
GET /api/v1/library 
[
  {
    "entitlementId": "ent-uuid",
    "productId": "product-uuid",
    "productName": "Pro Pack",
    "fileName": "pack.zip",
    "downloadToken": "tok-uuid",
    "downloadCount": 0,
    "maxDownloads": 5,
    "remainingDownloads": 5,
    "expiresAt": "2027-05-01T00:00:00Z",
    "active": true,
    "grantedByOrder": "order-uuid",
    "grantedBySubscription": null
  }
]
GET /api/v1/library/{token}/download
  • Rejects expired/exhausted downloads.
  • Increments the download count and returns a short-lived signed /api/v1/library/asset?... URL plus its expiry and remaining count.
  • The raw asset URL is never returned in JSON; the signed endpoint validates the HMAC/expiry and redirects to the asset.

Subscription entitlements have a higher download limit (50) and expire at the end of the current paid period. Canceled/PAST_DUE/expired subscriptions no longer expose active downloads and their entitlements are removed on cancellation/expiry; one-off order entitlements allow 5 downloads and expire after one year. Order cancellation/full refund revokes order-based entitlements immediately.

Other operations:

  • GET /api/v1/admin/subscriptions — List all subscriptions

docs.title: Tax Engine
docs.text: Tax zones, classes, rules and exemptions resolved per order line.

docs.title: Resolution order
docs.text:
1. Customer/business exemption (active, matching country or global, not expired) → zero tax.
  2. A matching tax_zone with isNexus = false → zero tax.
  3. The most specific active rule for the destination country:
  4. zone-scoped beats country-wide
  5. class-scoped beats class-agnostic
  6. category-scoped beats category-agnostic
  7. then highest priority, then oldest rule.
  8. The assigned product tax class default rate/mode.
  9. Application default (TAX_DEFAULT_RATE, default 5%).

A rule is only eligible when its zone/class/category (when set) matches the line.

docs.title: Inclusive vs exclusive
docs.text:
• Exclusive (default): the line amount is net; tax is added to the order total.
  • Inclusive: the line amount is gross; tax is carved out (net = gross / (1 + rate)). The order total does not add inclusive tax again.

docs.title: Wishlist
docs.text: Save products, check membership and move items to the cart.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
All Wishlist endpoints require Bearer token authentication. Include the access token in the Authorization header:

Authorization: Bearer <your_access_token>

docs.title: Wishlist Endpoints
docs.text: Method Endpoint Description Authentication Required POST /api/v1/wishlists Add a product to wishlist Yes GET /api/v1/wishlists Retrieve user's wishlist items (Paginated) Yes GET /api/v1/wishlists/check Check if a product is in wishlist Yes POST /api/v1/wishlists/move-to-cart Move a wishlist product into the cart Yes DELETE /api/v1/wishlists/remove Remove a product from wishlist Yes GET /api/v1/wishlists/ids List wishlisted product IDs Yes

docs.title: 1. Add Product to Wishlist
docs.text: POST /api/v1/wishlists Parameter Type Required Description productId string Yes UUID of the product to add to wishlist

docs.title: 2. Get Wishlist Items
docs.text: GET /api/v1/wishlists Parameter Type Required Description limit number No Maximum number of items to return (default: 20) offset number No Number of items to skip for pagination (default: 0)

docs.title: 3. Check Product in Wishlist
docs.text: GET /api/v1/wishlists/check Parameter Type Required Description productId string Yes UUID of the product to check

docs.title: 4. Move Product to Cart
docs.text: POST /api/v1/wishlists/move-to-cart Parameter Type Required Description productId string Yes UUID of the wishlist product to move quantity number No Quantity to add (default: 1)

docs.title: Request
docs.text:
curl -X 'POST' \
  'http://localhost:8080/api/v1/wishlists/move-to-cart?productId=6c5078d3-f8e3-4c88-9afe-48b5423c664f&quantity=1' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <access_token>'

Returns the updated cart summary (201 Created).

docs.title: 5. Remove Product from Wishlist
docs.text: DELETE /api/v1/wishlists/remove Parameter Type Required Description productId string Yes UUID of the product to remove from wishlist

docs.title: Error Handling
docs.text: This API follows industry-standard error handling patterns (Stripe, GitHub, OpenAI):

docs.title: Success Responses
docs.text:
• HTTP status code indicates success (200, 201, 204)
  • Response body contains data directly (no wrapper object)
  • No isSuccess or statusCode fields needed

docs.title: Error Responses
docs.text:
Standard Error (400/401/403/404/500): 

{
  "message": "Error description"
}

Validation Error (400): 

{
  "message": "Validation failed",
  "errors": [
    {"field": "email", "message": "Invalid email format"},
    {"field": "password", "message": "Password must be at least 8 characters"}
  ]
}

docs.title: Common Error Codes
docs.text:
Status Code Description Example Message 400 Bad Request "Invalid email or password" 401 Unauthorized "Authentication required" 403 Forbidden "Insufficient permissions" 404 Not Found "Product not found" 409 Conflict "User already exists with this email" 500 Internal Server Error "Internal server error"

All error messages are centralized and consistent across all endpoints.
